props.title: Paris Is Burning
props.initialSlug: Documentary about NYC's drag ball culture

sections.content: Paris Is Burning revolutionized documentary filmmaking by immersing viewers in New York's vibrant 1980s ballroom culture. Director Jennie Livingston captured the fierce competition, elaborate performances, and found families within the Black and Latino LGBTQ+ community when most mainstream media ignored or stigmatized these voices. The film's raw exploration of voguing, drag balls, and "realness" competitions directly influenced pop culture, from Madonna's "Vogue" to RuPaul's Drag Race (2009-present). The documentary's lasting impact shows in films like Moonlight (2016) and Pose (2018-2021), which built on its themes of chosen family and self-expression. The Queen|1968|This groundbreaking documentary follows drag queens preparing for the 1967 Miss All-America Camp Beauty Contest, providing crucial historical context for the ball scene|Criterion Tongues Untied|1989|Marlon Riggs' experimental documentary explores Black gay identity and expression through poetry, personal testimony and performance|Kanopy Strike a Pose|2016|Documentary following Madonna's backup dancers from her Blonde Ambition tour, many of whom came from the ballroom scene|Netflix

The film's exploration of gender performance and identity influenced a wave of New Queer Cinema in the 1990s. The Adventures of Priscilla, Queen of the Desert (1994) and To Wong Foo, Thanks for Everything! Julie Newmar (1995) brought drag culture to mainstream audiences, while documentaries like The Salt Mines (1990) and The Transformation (1995) continued examining the lives of trans women of color. These films challenged conventional documentary approaches by giving marginalized subjects direct voice and agency. SUBHEAD: Impact on Modern LGBTQ+ Cinema

Contemporary films continue building on Paris Is Burning's legacy. Tangerine (2015) captures trans sex workers' lives with similar intimacy and authenticity. Kiki (2016) revisits New York's ballroom scene 25 years later, showing how the community evolved while facing ongoing challenges. Port Authority (2019) incorporates ballroom culture into its romantic narrative, demonstrating how the scene's influence has spread beyond documentary into narrative storytelling.
